note: GENERATED by scripts/generate-part-two.mjs from the core lesson — do not hand-edit.
contentObjective: I can draw polygons from their vertex coordinates on the coordinate plane, and use coordinates to find side lengths and solve perimeter and area problems.
languageObjective: I can explain how I found a distance using the words vertices, coordinates, and absolute value.

vocabulary.definition: A corner point of a polygon, named by an ordered pair on the coordinate plane.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un punto de esquina de un polígono, nombrado por un par ordenado en el plano de coordenadas.
vocabulary.visual: The park's corner at (2, 4) — one corner, named by an ordered pair.

examples.text: (5, 4), where two sides of the park meet
examples.why: It is a corner, and a coordinate pair names it.
That is a side; a vertex is the point where sides meet.

vocabulary.definition: A closed figure made of line segments; on the plane you draw it by plotting the vertices and connecting them in order.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura cerrada hecha de segmentos; en el plano se dibuja marcando los vértices y conectándolos en orden.
vocabulary.example: Plot the four points, connect them, and the rectangle appears.
vocabulary.visual: Plot (2, 4), (5, 4), (5, −4), (2, −4) and join them — a rectangle appears.
vocabulary.cloze: A closed figure made of line segments is a ___.

examples.text: Four plotted vertices joined in order into a closed rectangle
examples.why: Straight sides, and the figure closes.

examples.text: Three points joined but left open
examples.why: An unclosed path is not a polygon.

vocabulary.definition: The total distance around a polygon — the sum of all its side lengths.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La distancia total alrededor de un polígono: la suma de todos sus lados.
vocabulary.cloze: The total distance around a polygon is its ___.

examples.text: Adding all four side lengths of the rectangle
examples.why: It measures the whole way around.
That gives area — the space inside, not the distance around.

vocabulary.definition: When two vertices share an x- or y-coordinate, the distance between them is the absolute difference of the other coordinates.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cuando dos vértices comparten una coordenada x o y, la distancia es la diferencia absoluta de las otras coordenadas.
vocabulary.visual: (2, 4) and (5, 4) share y, so the side is |5 − 2| = 3 units.
vocabulary.cloze: When two vertices share a coordinate, subtract the other and take the ___ ___.

examples.text: |4 − (−4)| = 8 for two vertices that share an x-value
examples.why: Same x means a vertical side, found by subtracting the y-values.
Losing the negative sign collapses the side to nothing.

vocabulary.definition: What one grid unit stands for in the real situation.

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Maria's Craft Store
revealWordProblem.text:
Maria, a craft store owner, plans to rent a location in a shopping center and is considering the two spaces shown on the grid. Each unit represents one foot, so each line on the grid represents 5 feet. Space A rents for $13.89 per square foot each month, and Space B rents for $13.49 per square foot each month. Maria wants to pay the lower total monthly rent.
Question: Which location would you recommend she rent?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: Two shop spaces drawn as polygons on a coordinate grid, labeled Space A and Space B, with vertices at 0 comma 0, 5 comma 35, 15 comma 35, 15 comma 0, and 39 comma 0.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Find each floor area from the grid by decomposing the polygon into rectangles and triangles and using the vertex coordinates for the side lengths. Multiply each area by its own rate — Space A by $13.89 and Space B by $13.49 — to get the total monthly rent for each. The lower rate does not decide it on its own: a bigger space at the lower rate can still cost more each month. Recommend the space with the lower total, and say what Maria gives up in floor area by choosing it.

questions.stem: Vertices (-4.5, 3) and (5, 3) share y = 3. What is the distance between them?
questions.explanation: They differ only in x: |5 − (−4.5)| = 5 + 4.5 = 9.5 units.
choiceFeedback: That subtracts 4.5 − 4 or similar — remember the point is at NEGATIVE 4.5, so the distance crosses zero.
That subtracts 5 − 3.5 or mixes an x with a y — use the two x-coordinates only.
That ignores the .5 on −4.5.
hints: Which coordinate is the same? Which differs?
Distance crosses zero: 4.5 to reach 0, then 5 more.
questions.stemEs: Los vértices (-4.5, 3) y (5, 3) comparten y = 3. ¿Cuál es la distancia entre ellos?
questions.explanationEs: Solo se diferencian en x: |5 − (−4.5)| = 5 + 4.5 = 9.5 unidades.
hintsEs: Los valores de x son −4.5 y 5.
La distancia cruza el cero: 4.5 para llegar a 0, luego 5 más.

questions.stem: Vertices (5, 3) and (5, -3.75) share x = 5. What is the distance between them?
questions.explanation: They differ only in y: |3 − (−3.75)| = 3 + 3.75 = 6.75 units.
choiceFeedback: That subtracts 3.75 − 3 as if both were on the same side of zero.
5 is the shared x-coordinate, not a distance.
That adds 5 + 3.75, mixing the shared x into the answer.
questions.stemEs: Los vértices (5, 3) y (5, -3.75) comparten x = 5. ¿Cuál es la distancia entre ellos?
questions.explanationEs: Solo se diferencian en y: |3 − (−3.75)| = 3 + 3.75 = 6.75 unidades.
hintsEs: Los valores de y son 3 y −3.75.
3 arriba del cero más 3.75 abajo del cero.

questions.stem: What is the perimeter of the rectangle with side lengths 9.5 and 6.75 units?
choiceFeedback: 16.25 is 9.5 + 6.75 — that walks only two of the four sides.
26 misses the decimal halves; recompute 19 + 13.5.
64.125 is 9.5 × 6.75 — that is the area, not the perimeter.
questions.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el perímetro del rectángulo con lados de 9.5 y 6.75 unidades?

steps: 1. Plot all given vertices and connect them in order to form the polygon
2. Find side lengths by counting grid units or using coordinate distance formulas
3. Perimeter = Sum of all side lengths; Area = Use standard polygon formulas
reviewHighlights.watchOut: Subtracting coordinates without the absolute value — from y = 3 down to y = −3.75 the distance is 3 + 3.75 = 6.75 units, not 3.75 − 3 = 0.75. Distances that cross zero are the whole reason the absolute value is there.

level1.stem: Why are two of the terms multiplied by 2 in the perimeter calculation?
choices: Because perimeter always doubles the area
Because there are two coordinates in each ordered pair
A rectangle's opposite sides are equal, so each length appears on two sides
level1.explanation: The two 9.5 sides and the two 6.75 sides each come in pairs — that is what the 2 counts.
choiceFeedback: Perimeter and area are different measurements; neither doubles the other.
The 2 counts sides, not coordinates.
No rounding is happening — 32.5 is exact.
hints: Walk the rectangle: how many 9.5 sides?
level1.stemEs: ¿Por qué dos de los términos se multiplican por 2 en el cálculo del perímetro?
level1.explanationEs: Los dos lados de 9.5 y los dos de 6.75 vienen en pares — eso es lo que cuenta el 2.
hintsEs: Recorre el rectángulo: ¿cuántos lados de 9.5 hay?

level1.stem: To draw a polygon from a list of vertices, you:
choices: Connect the points in any random order
Plot each ordered pair, then connect them in order with segments
level1.explanation: Graph the points on the plane and connect them in order — the closed figure that appears is the polygon.
choiceFeedback: One point cannot make a polygon.
Random order can cross the segments and make a different figure.
Adding coordinates gives a number, not a shape.
hints: What did the deck say to do first?
level1.stemEs: Para dibujar un polígono a partir de una lista de vértices, tú:
level1.explanationEs: Ubica los puntos en el plano y conéctalos en orden — la figura cerrada que aparece es el polígono.
hintsEs: ¿Qué dijo la presentación que había que hacer primero?

level1.stem: A square has vertices (1, 2), (6, 2), (6, -3), (1, -3). Find one side length and the perimeter.
level1.modelAnswer: From (1, 2) to (6, 2): |6 − 1| = 5 units. A square has four equal sides, so the perimeter is 4 × 5 = 20 units.
sentenceStems: So one side is ___ , and the perimeter is ___ .
level1.stemEs: Un cuadrado tiene vértices (1, 2), (6, 2), (6, -3), (1, -3). Halla la longitud de un lado y el perímetro.

level2.stem: The park's marked vertices are 3 units apart and each unit is 100 feet. What is the park's width?
choiceFeedback: 3 is the number of UNITS — the scale turns units into feet.
That multiplies by 10 instead of 100.
That adds 3 + 100 instead of multiplying.
hints: What does one unit stand for?
level2.stemEs: Los vértices marcados del parque están a 3 unidades de distancia y cada unidad son 100 pies. ¿Cuál es el ancho del parque?

level2.stem: The park's area must be 240,000 sq ft and its width is 300 ft. What is its length?
choiceFeedback: 720 comes from 240,000 ÷ 333 or a slip; recompute 240,000 ÷ 300.
That divides by 3 instead of 300 — keep the zeros with the width.
That adds the width to the area — area and length combine by division here.
hints: Area = length × width. Solve for length.
level2.stemEs: El área del parque debe ser 240,000 pies cuadrados y su ancho es 300 pies. ¿Cuál es su largo?
hintsEs: Área = largo × ancho. Despeja el largo.

level2.stem: The length is 800 feet and each unit represents 100 feet. How many units long is the park on the map?
choiceFeedback: That divides by 1,000 instead of 100.
That divides by 10 instead of 100.
That forgets the scale entirely — the map is not drawn in feet.
hints: Feet to units: divide by what one unit stands for.
level2.stemEs: El largo es 800 pies y cada unidad representa 100 pies. ¿Cuántas unidades de largo mide el parque en el mapa?
hintsEs: De pies a unidades: divide entre lo que representa una unidad.

level2.stem: The known vertices of the park are at (2, 4) and (5, 4), and the length runs DOWNWARD 8 units. Where are the other two vertices?
level2.explanation: 8 units below y = 4 is y = 4 − 8 = −4, keeping each x the same: (2, −4) and (5, −4).
choiceFeedback: (2, 12) moves UP 8 units instead of down.
y = −8 would be 12 units below y = 4, not 8.
Those move sideways along x instead of down.
level2.stemEs: Los vértices conocidos del parque están en (2, 4) y (5, 4), y el largo va HACIA ABAJO 8 unidades. ¿Dónde están los otros dos vértices?
level2.explanationEs: 8 unidades debajo de y = 4 es y = 4 − 8 = −4, manteniendo igual cada x: (2, −4) y (5, −4).
hintsEs: Hacia abajo significa restar de y.
Las coordenadas x se quedan igual.

level2.stem: A rectangle has vertices (-3, 2), (4, 2), (4, -1), (-3, -1). What is its perimeter?
choiceFeedback: 10 is 7 + 3 — only two of the four sides.
13 misreads one of the distances; recompute both using absolute differences.
21 is 7 × 3 — the area, not the perimeter.
hints: Find both side lengths from the coordinates first.
level2.stemEs: Un rectángulo tiene vértices (-3, 2), (4, 2), (4, -1), (-3, -1). ¿Cuál es su perímetro?
level2.explanationEs: Ancho |4 − (−3)| = 7, alto |2 − (−1)| = 3, así que P = 2(7) + 2(3) = 20 unidades.
hintsEs: Halla primero las dos longitudes de los lados a partir de las coordenadas.

level3.stem: A rectangle has vertices at (1, 1), (7, 1), (7, 5), and (1, 5). What is its perimeter?
choiceFeedback: That adds one of each side. Each length appears twice around a rectangle.
That doubles the horizontal side only. The two vertical sides of 4 units each still count.
That is the AREA, 6 times 4, in square units. Perimeter adds the four side lengths.
level3.explanation: The horizontal sides are |7 − 1| = 6 units and the vertical sides are |5 − 1| = 4 units. Perimeter = 2(6) + 2(4) = 20 units.

level3.stem: Maria is choosing between two store spaces on a grid where each unit is 1 foot and each grid line is 5 feet apart. Space A is a rectangle 25 ft by 40 ft; Space B is 30 ft by 30 ft. Which has more floor area?
choices: Space A — 1,000 sq ft vs 900 sq ft
Space B — 900 sq ft vs 850 sq ft
Space B — because a square always beats a rectangle
level3.explanation: A: 25 × 40 = 1,000 sq ft. B: 30 × 30 = 900 sq ft. Space A has 100 more square feet.
choiceFeedback: B is 900, but A is 1,000 — recompute 25 × 40.
Shape does not decide area; the dimensions do.
level3.stemEs: María escoge entre dos locales en una cuadrícula donde cada unidad es 1 pie y cada línea está a 5 pies de distancia. El espacio A es un rectángulo de 25 pies por 40 pies; el espacio B es de 30 pies por 30 pies. ¿Cuál tiene más área de piso?
level3.explanationEs: A: 25 × 40 = 1,000 pies cuadrados. B: 30 × 30 = 900 pies cuadrados. El espacio A tiene 100 pies cuadrados más.

level3.stem: A square has vertices (a, b) and (a, b + s) on one side. Which operation gives the side length for ANY values?
choices: Subtract the y-coordinates and take the absolute value
level3.explanation: Same x means the side is vertical, and |(b + s) − b| = |s| — subtraction with absolute value works for every case.
choiceFeedback: Adding coordinates has no geometric meaning here.
A product of coordinates is not a distance.
An average finds a midpoint, not a length.
hints: Which coordinate changes along the side?
Distance = absolute difference of the changing coordinate.
level3.stemEs: Un cuadrado tiene los vértices (a, b) y (a, b + s) en un lado. ¿Cuál operación da la longitud del lado para CUALQUIER valor?
level3.explanationEs: La misma x significa que el lado es vertical, y |(b + s) − b| = |s| — la resta con valor absoluto funciona en todos los casos.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál coordenada cambia a lo largo del lado?
Distancia = diferencia absoluta de la coordenada que cambia.

level3.stem: The park design used width from coordinates, then length from the area, then the scale to place the missing vertices. Design your own version: pick an area and a scale, mark two vertices, and show where the other two go.
level3.modelAnswer: My park has area 60,000 sq ft with each unit = 100 ft. I mark vertices at (1, 5) and (3, 5) — 2 units apart, so width 200 ft. Length = 60,000 ÷ 200 = 300 ft = 3 units, so the other vertices go at (1, 2) and (3, 2), 3 units below.
sentenceStems: My area is ___ and each unit is ___ .
So the other vertices are at ___ .
level3.stemEs: El diseño del parque usó el ancho de las coordenadas, luego el largo del área, y luego la escala para ubicar los vértices que faltaban. Diseña tu propia versión: escoge un área y una escala, marca dos vértices y muestra dónde van los otros dos.

level3.stem: Check the deck's perimeter of 32.5 units a DIFFERENT way than adding the four sides in order.
level3.modelAnswer: Instead of walking the sides, I can use the formula P = 2(l + w): 2(9.5 + 6.75) = 2(16.25) = 32.5 units. Both methods must agree, which is what makes it a check.
level3.stemEs: Revisa el perímetro de 32.5 unidades de la terraza de una manera DISTINTA a sumar los cuatro lados en orden.

tool.title: Perimeter of the Rectangle (−3, 2), (4, 2), (4, −1), (−3, −1)
tool.caption: The two horizontal sides are each |4 − (−3)| = 7 units and the two vertical sides are each |2 − (−1)| = 3 units, so the perimeter is 7 + 7 + 3 + 3 = 20 units.
